newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Qian urges Britain to cooperate on HK.
newsitem.headline: China's Qian urges Britain to cooperate on HK.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Saturday he hoped for more cooperation in talks this month with his British counterpart amid London protests over Beijing's plan to roll back Hong Kong's civil rights.

Qian is to meet British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind this month in Singapore, where Rifkind plans to bring up concerns over the future of Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 this year.
"I hope the meeting will take place in a constructive atmosphere, and that there will be more cooperation and less trouble," the Xinhua news agency quoted Qian as saying.

Beijing's proposal to abolish or amend 25 Hong Kong laws and ordinances after the handover, such as ones on civil rights and public assembly, has drawn criticism from Britain and the territory's democracy activists.
The China-appointed Preparatory Committee that is handling the change of sovereignty endorsed on Saturday Beijing's plans in a move that Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten called "disturbing".
Washington has expressed concern over the proposals and Britain has summoned the Chinese ambassador to lodge a protest.
Beijing has defended the proposed changes, saying Hong Kong's future mini-constitution, the Basic Law, provides ample guarantees of civil liberties and fundamental freedoms.
Qian urged British cooperation in the handover process, Xinhua said.
"Keeping Hong Kong's original laws basically unchanged is crucial for the region's long-term stability and prosperity, and is the responsibility of both China and Britain," Qian said.
